text:
sarah: Hey team — onboarding Astral-6B (QAT/int8) into the eval harness. CI keeps failing with a collate-length-mismatch and our rouge/bleu numbers look noisy. Repro: a simple prompt with an em-dash gives different token counts locally vs CI. Anyone seen unicode split issues before?

alex: Which tokenizer are you using? BPE vs byte-level matters a lot for weird punctuation.

sarah: It's a bytelevel-bpe variant from upstream. We converted the files with hf-tokenizer-convert and used the repo's tokenizer config. Example: `hello—world` encodes to 5 tokens locally, but CI encodes to 6, which causes batched collate asserts. Logs: ```ERROR collate.py: AssertionError: batch sizes differ [8,7]
  File "collate.py", line 42, in collate_batch
    assert all(len(x)==len(batch[0]) for x in batch)```

jen: Hmm. Could be normalization differences (NFC vs NFKC) between tokenizers on different images. We had similar flakiness with en-dash vs em-dash last year. Quick diff: `pip freeze | grep tokenizers` on CI vs local?

mike: Also check the tokenizers lib version and the huggingface tokenizers backend (rust) — different patch releases changed how some unicode codepoints are treated.

sarah: CI image uses tokenizers==0.15.2, local dev is 0.16.0. Didn't think a patch would change em-dash splitting.

alex: Two practical fixes: 1) Normalize inputs in the eval harness pre-tokenize step (unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)). 2) Add a fallback tokenization path: if batch collate fails, retry with a conservative `legacy_tokenize` that forces byte-level behavior.

jen: I can throw together a unit test covering the em-dash and en-dash cases and add it to the eval-runner test suite. Test snippet: ```python
import unicodedata
print(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', 'a—b'))
# expected: 'a—b' (normalized form)```

mike: Also callout: QAT/int8 can change token generation slightly at decode time (length, spacing), which can bump rouge/bleu a bit. If the tokenization mismatch is fixed, rerun float16 vs q8f vs q4f comparisons to isolate quantization regression.

sarah: Good point. After normalization patch we should run a matrix: float16 + q8f + q4f on small eval set and compare generation lengths and rouge-L deltas.

alex: I'll open a quick PR to add NFKC normalization + a safe fallback for the collate step. Also adding a small metric to the dashboard: `tokenization-delta` = fraction of examples with differing token counts between Ci and local reference.

ci-bot: @alex requested a rerun of CI (build #3421).

eval-bot: CI queued: eval-suite / runner-integration / #3421.

ci-bot: Build #3421 finished: SUCCESS. However eval-suite reported 1 failing eval: `summarization/weekly-5k` with rouge-L delta +0.032 for q4f vs float16.

mike: That rouge bump is borderline; could be decode-length change from quantization. We should check length histograms and n-gram overlap; if decode lengths differ systematically, we might need a length-normalized metric or a penalized-variance check.

sarah: Plan of attack: 1) land normalization + collate fallback PR (jen will add unit tests), 2) run 3-way quant matrix on a 500-sample subset, 3) add dashboard panels for tokenization-delta and decode-length-histogram, 4) if q4f still regresses, run ablation on activation clipping vs calibration dataset.

jen: I'll create the PR and include the test cases (em-dash, emoji split, CJK punctuation). Will tag you @sarah for verification. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/??? (WIP) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: Thanks — once CI passes with the new tests, let's promote the unique failing sample to a monitored alert so we catch this early during future model onboarding.

mike: One more note: add a small fuzz test to the tokenizer conversion step in CI (random unicode sequences) to guard against upstream tokenizer changes. Took us a while last time.

sarah: Agreed. I'll queue the matrix runs after the PR lands and post the results here. Appreciate the quick triage! :thumbsup:
